business_rules: Email addresses are case‑insensitive for lookup; a person joining two organizations uses the same account.
Failed email delivery should not cause underlying assignment or mention to be rolled back.

functions.signature: def register_account(email_address: str, password: str) -> account_record
functions.purpose: Creates a new user account; requires email verification before the account becomes fully active.

functions.signature: def request_password_reset(email_address: str) -> reset_token
functions.purpose: Generates a temporary password‑reset token without revealing whether the email exists; token is short‑lived.

functions.signature: def check_auth(user_id: str, action: str, resource: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Verifies that the given user is authenticated and authorized to perform the specified action on the resource.

business_rules: Organizations are isolated; a member of one organization cannot access another regardless of email overlap.
Roles follow a hierarchy: owner, administrator, member; only one owner at a time.
Ownership transfer requires the new owner to already belong to the organization.
Data visibility inherits from parent objects to avoid per‑child authorization rules.

functions.signature: def create_organization(name: str, identifier: Optional[str] = None) -> organization_id
functions.purpose: Creates a new organization; the first user becomes the initial owner.

functions.signature: def invite_member(email_address: str, organization_id: str) -> invitation_record
functions.purpose: Sends an invitation to join an organization; invitations expire and can be revoked.

functions.signature: def transfer_ownership(organization_id: str, new_owner_id: str) -> success_status
functions.purpose: Transfers organization ownership to an existing member; records the action in activity history.

business_rules: Projects can be created, completed, or archived; archived projects remain inspectable but are hidden from primary lists.
Work items have statuses (not_completed, in_progress, completed) and can move back to active state.
Historical activity is append‑only; users cannot rewrite past events.
Comments are stored as untrusted input and must be escaped before rendering.
Notifications are generated for assignments, mentions, and follows; email failures do not roll back the underlying event.
Search respects organization and project access boundaries; users cannot discover inaccessible projects.
Dashboard counts are derived from currently accessible data, not from a permanent truth source.
Due dates are calendar days independent of viewer timezone.
Concurrency strategy: last‑write is acceptable for simple fields; stronger guarantees for membership changes or ownership transfer.

functions.signature: def create_project(name: str, description: str, creator_id: str) -> project_id
functions.purpose: Creates a new project; the creator normally becomes the initial project owner.

functions.signature: def create_work_item(project_id: str, title: str, status: str, priority: int, due_date: Optional[date] = None) -> work_item_id
functions.purpose: Creates a work item belonging to a project with required fields and optional due date.

functions.signature: def add_comment(work_item_id: str, author_id: str, body: str) -> comment_id
functions.purpose: Adds an untrusted comment to a work item; content must be escaped.

functions.signature: def upload_attachment(resource_id: str, file_content: bytes, filename: str) -> attachment_id
functions.purpose: Attaches a file to a work item or comment; filename is not trusted as a filesystem path.

functions.signature: def search_operational_content(query: str, scope: authorization_scope) -> search_results
functions.purpose: Searches across operational content while enforcing organization and project access boundaries.

business_rules: Uploaded files may initially be in a processing state before becoming available for download.
Filenames must be sanitized to prevent path‑traversal (e.g., '../../' patterns).
File content is never auto‑interpreted as HTML or executable code; appropriate content‑disposition is applied.
Authentication and authorization are required before serving private files.
Temporary download URLs have a limited lifetime and must expire.
File upload size limits are enforced before data transfer begins.
Identical filenames from different users are allowed; each file is stored with a distinct internal identifier.

functions.signature: def upload_file(user_id: str, organization_id: str, file: File) -> UploadResponse
functions.purpose: Handles user‑initiated file upload after validation and size checks.

functions.signature: def download_file(user_id: str, organization_id: str, file_id: str) -> FileResponse
functions.purpose: Serves a file to an authorized user with proper content‑disposition.

functions.signature: def validate_file_name(file_name: str) -> bool
functions.purpose: Ensures the filename does not contain disallowed patterns such as path traversal.

functions.signature: def enforce_upload_limit(file_size: int) -> None
functions.purpose: Raises an error if the file exceeds configured size limits.

functions.signature: def generate_temporary_download_url(file_id: str, expires_in_seconds: int) -> str
functions.purpose: Creates a short‑lived URL for downloading a file.

functions.signature: def content_disposition(file: File) -> str
functions.purpose: Generates a safe Content‑Disposition header to prevent inline execution of uploaded content.

business_rules: Background jobs must include target organization and resource identifiers independent of the browser session.
Jobs may be retried, but a job that repeatedly fails must not retry forever without operator visibility.
Failed background work must be investigable via operational tooling.
Email sending, search indexing, and notification generation are performed asynchronously.
Retry logic limits the number of attempts to avoid infinite loops.

functions.signature: def process_background_job(job_id: str, organization_id: str, resource_id: str) -> JobResult
functions.purpose: Executes a queued background job for the given organization and resource.

functions.signature: def retry_job(job_id: str) -> RetryResult
functions.purpose: Attempts to re‑execute a failed background job respecting retry limits.

functions.signature: def get_failed_jobs() -> List[JobInfo]
functions.purpose: Returns information about background jobs that have exceeded retry limits or failed permanently.

rules: API authorization must enforce organization boundary beyond web interface.
Filename such as ../../something must never become direct filesystem location.
Uploaded file content not automatically interpreted as HTML or executable code.
Authentication must be applied before generating or serving private file access.
Prevent path traversal by sanitizing file names; disallow '../../' patterns.
Do not auto‑interpret file content as HTML or executable code; enforce content‑disposition.
Require authentication and authorization before serving private files.
Background jobs must identify target organization and resource independent of session.
Representing events should have unambiguous timezone interpretation.
Relative labels generated using relevant user or organization context, not stored as text.
Transitions should not cause logic to assume every calendar day has exactly same number of hours.
Temporary download URLs must expire after a limited lifetime.
Operations that modify resources should allow retries without creating duplicate logical records.
Stronger guarantees necessary for membership changes or ownership transfer to prevent conflicting owners.
Background job processing should handle concurrent execution safely.
Sending email, updating search indexes, generating notifications processed asynchronously.
Jobs that repeatedly fail should not retry forever without visibility to operators.
Provide operational tooling to investigate failed background jobs.
Limit retry attempts for background jobs to avoid infinite loops.
Historical information remains intelligible even if actor display name changes or account deactivated.
Removal should not rewrite old activity or cause work items to silently disappear.
Safe to expose to clients. Authorization must never depend on difficulty of guessing identifier.
Ordering needs to be stable enough that records are not randomly skipped or repeated.
User with no assigned work should receive useful empty state rather than technical error.
Mobile-specific behavior not part of initial product definition. Underlying API should not make mobile clients impossible later.
